answer:
The exact number is
\[
\boxed{\frac{2^{1000}+4\cdot 2^{200}}{5}}.
\]

To see this, let
\[
F(x)=\prod_{k=1}^{1000}(1+x^k).
\]
The coefficient of \(x^m\) counts subsets with sum \(m\), including the empty set when \(m=0\).

Let \(\zeta=e^{2\pi i/5}\). Since
\[
\frac15\sum_{j=0}^{4}\zeta^{jm}
=
\begin{cases}
1,&5\mid m,\\
0,&5\nmid m,
\end{cases}
\]
the desired count is
\[
\frac15\sum_{j=0}^{4}F(\zeta^j).
\]

We have \(F(1)=2^{1000}\). For each \(j=1,2,3,4\), every residue modulo \(5\) occurs exactly \(200\) times among \(1,\ldots,1000\), so
\[
F(\zeta^j)=\left(\prod_{r=0}^{4}(1+\zeta^{jr})\right)^{200}.
\]
Multiplication by \(j\) permutes the residues modulo \(5\), and evaluating
\[
\prod_{r=0}^{4}(t-\zeta^r)=t^5-1
\]
at \(t=-1\) gives \(\prod_{r=0}^{4}(1+\zeta^r)=2\). Thus all four remaining terms equal \(2^{200}\), yielding the stated answer.
